name: mcp-teams

tools.name: get_version
tools.description: Shows the mcp-teams server version and build, the browser extension version, and whether Teams is reachable (which of its services have a session). restartNeeded: true means mcp-teams was updated on disk while this server still runs the old code: the user should reconnect it (in Claude Code: /mcp) and reload the extension.

tools.name: reload_extension
tools.description: Reloads the mcp-teams browser extension from disk, e.g. after an update changed it, and waits until it is connected again. Returns the extension version before and after. Refused while a send confirmation window is open.

tools.name: api_traffic
tools.description: Lists the API endpoints the open Teams tab called while recording was on: method, host, path, status, which headers were sent (names only, never values) and the auth scheme. Used to find out which API Teams uses for a feature. Recording is off until you turn it on: first call with record: true, then click through the feature in Teams, then call again to list what it called. Recording stops after 30 minutes or with record: false; what was recorded stays until clear.

record.description: true: start recording the Teams tab's API calls (for 30 minutes); false: stop recording. Leave out to only list

filter.description: Only requests whose host or path contains this text

clear.description: Clear the recorded traffic after returning it

tools.name: list_teams
tools.description: Lists the teams you are a member of, each with its channels. Group chats and meeting chats are not teams, even when they are named like one: list_chats lists those. Use 'Team/Channel' or a channel id as the conversation for read_messages and send_message. The list may be up to a minute old (see refresh). Needs a Teams tab open in the browser: without one it fails at once.

include_ids.description: Also return team and channel ids (long; 'Team/Channel' names are enough to address channels)

refresh.description: Read the list from Teams again instead of reusing the one from the last minute: e.g. right after a chat was created or joined elsewhere, or for the current unread state

tools.name: list_chats
tools.description: Lists your chats (1:1, group and meeting chats), most recent first, with their title (or the other members' names), the last message and whether it is unread. Returns ids for read_messages and send_message. The list may be up to a minute old, so the last message and unread state can lag; pass refresh: true for the current ones. Needs a Teams tab open in the browser: without one it fails at once.

query.description: Only chats whose title or a member's name contains these words

refresh.description: Read the list from Teams again instead of reusing the one from the last minute: e.g. right after a chat was created or joined elsewhere, or for the current unread state

tools.name: read_messages
tools.description: Reads the latest messages of a chat or channel, oldest first: sender, time, text (formatting removed), files shared and reactions. In channels, replies are nested under their post (a reply whose post is on an older page comes on its own, with replyTo). To read further back, pass the returned olderCursor as `cursor` (with the same conversation and reply_to); it is there whenever older history exists, so keep paging while it is returned. A page usually costs one or two Teams requests, but one call reads at most 20 pages of Teams history: it may then return fewer messages than asked, even none, with `truncated: true`, a note and an olderCursor to go on. `before` (a time) also works but re-reads from the newest message each call, so it hits that limit sooner. Give cursor or before, not both. With reply_to, reads one channel post's whole thread.

conversation.description: Which chat or channel: its id from list_chats/list_teams (19:…), 'Team/Channel' (e.g. 'Engineering/General'), a chat title, or a person's name for your 1:1 chat with them. A name must match exactly one conversation, otherwise the matches are listed.

limit.description: How many messages (channel: posts, each with its replies)

cursor.description: Continue from olderCursor of a previous call on the same conversation (opaque; pass it exactly as returned)

before.description: Only messages older than this time (ISO 8601, e.g. olderBefore from a previous call). Prefer cursor for paging

reply_to.description: Channel only: the id of a post, to read its thread

include_system.description: Also return events such as members added or calls started

max_length.description: Maximum length of each message's text

tools.name: list_meetings
tools.description: Lists your Teams meetings (each scheduled meeting or recurring series has a meeting chat), most recent activity first: subject, scheduled time (for a series, its first occurrence), organizer, whether a transcript exists, and whether another organization hosted it (`external`: its chat and recordings are usually no longer readable afterwards). The list may be up to a minute old (see refresh). Use get_meeting for the calls held and who attended, read_transcript for what was said, read_messages for the meeting chat.

query.description: Only meetings whose subject or organizer contains these words

refresh.description: Read the list from Teams again instead of reusing the one from the last minute: e.g. right after a chat was created or joined elsewhere, or for the current unread state

tools.name: get_meeting
tools.description: One meeting with the calls held in it, newest first (a recurring meeting has one per occurrence): when it started and ended, who joined, the recording's link, and whether there is a transcript.

meeting.description: Which meeting: its chat id from list_meetings (19:meeting_…) or its title. A title must match exactly one meeting chat.

tools.name: read_transcript
tools.description: What was said in a meeting, from its Teams transcript: lines '[hh:mm:ss] Speaker: text', plus how long each speaker talked. Reads the latest call with a transcript unless `session` names another. Long transcripts are cut at max_length; pass the returned continueFrom as `from` to read on. Transcripts are stored in the organizer's OneDrive, so this may open OneDrive in a background tab.

meeting.description: Which meeting: its chat id from list_meetings (19:meeting_…) or its title. A title must match exactly one meeting chat.

session.description: Which call: its callId from get_meeting, or its start date/time prefix (e.g. '2026-10-06')

from.description: Start at this point of the meeting, 'hh:mm:ss' or 'mm:ss'

max_length.description: Most characters of transcript to return

tools.name: search_transcripts
tools.description: Finds what was said in meetings: the transcript lines containing all words of the query, each with the line before it, from the most recent meetings with a transcript (or one meeting). Then read_transcript with `from` reads around a match.

query.description: Words that must all appear in a line (case-insensitive)

meeting.description: Which meeting: its chat id from list_meetings (19:meeting_…) or its title. A title must match exactly one meeting chat.

meetings.description: How many of the most recent meetings with a transcript to search

tools.name: search_messages
tools.description: Searches all your Teams chats and channels with Microsoft Search, like the search box in Teams. Returns matching messages with their conversation id (for read_messages), sender, time and a highlighted excerpt.

query.description: Words to search for; Teams search syntax such as from:alice or "exact phrase" works too

tools.name: find_people
tools.description: Looks people up by name or email in your organization (and people you work with), as in Teams' people picker: name, email, job title, department, office.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Asks to post a message in an existing chat or channel (conversation), to reply to a channel post, or to start a chat with people (to): one person for a 1:1 chat, several for a group chat. If a chat with exactly those people already exists, the message goes there. The extension shows a confirmation window with the message, where it goes and who is in a new chat; nothing is posted, and no chat is created, unless the user clicks Send there. Returns whether it was sent, and when Teams recorded it (time). A sent result can have time: null with a timeNote when Teams accepted the message but its answer, or the time in it, couldn't be read: it was still posted, so don't send it again. Plain text; line breaks are kept and links become clickable.

conversation.description: Which chat or channel: its id from list_chats/list_teams (19:…), 'Team/Channel' (e.g. 'Engineering/General'), a chat title, or a person's name for your 1:1 chat with them. A name must match exactly one conversation, otherwise the matches are listed.

to.description: Instead of conversation: the people to chat with, by name or email (e.g. ['김민준', 'ana@example.com']). Each must match exactly one person in your organization, otherwise the matches are listed.

title.description: With to (two or more people): a title for the new group chat

reply_to.description: Channel only: the id of the post to reply to (from read_messages). Without it, a new post is started.

subject.description: Channel only: a subject for a new post
